segments.text: The air itself freezes, and falls.
Twelve o'clock, noon: the Sun vanishes.
A year later, the average temperature on Earth's surface would be around minus seventy degrees Celsius.
It settles at around minus two hundred and forty degrees. That's colder than Pluto is today.
Nitrogen and oxygen drift down as snow and frost, and lie on the ground in a thin, frozen layer.
The air... falls down? So there's no sky anymore?
No sky. No wind. Just stars, all the way down to the ground.
